text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Survey data presented to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission by the Metal Trades Federation of Unions suggests wages pressures from collective bargaining may ease during this year. The data showed union leaders lowered their expectations on the short and medium-term outlook for inflation late last year. Page 2.

Private research firms, pollsters, universities, and independent economic analysts conducting surveys, studies or market research earned more than A$22 million in Commonwealth consultancy funding in 1995-96. The biggest Government spender was the Department of Health and Family Services, which spent A$9.3 million on research. Page 4.

Prime Minister John Howard was not supportive of dramatic tax reform yesterday, claiming that it was not a cure all for the economy and while stating that he would consider it, he said tax reform lay beyond the next election. He also criticised plans to introduce a GST, saying the Australian public was still hostile to the idea. Page 5.

Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday that he is considering legislation to overturn the High Court's Wik decision. Following a summit of State and Territory leaders he said that a plan to extinguish native title under common law and replace it with statutory rights of Aboriginal access to farms was an option being seriously considered. John Howard meets with Aboriginal leaders on February 3 and 6. Page 1.
THE AUSTRALIAN

After his meeting with state and territory leaders, Prime Minister John Howard has been criticised by prominent Aboriginal leaders for his suggestion that changes may have to be made to the Racial Discrimination Act in response to the High Court Wik nativ title decision. Cape York Land Council adviser Noel Pearson said anyone who claims the Act must be interfered with and that solutions can be found outside the Act, must be a racist. Page 1.

Rosemary and Mark Sims returned to their home in Mount View Road, Ferny Creek, in the Dandenong ranges east of Melbourne yesterday, to find it completely burned down. While Ms Sims said it was the personal belongings such as wedding rings and old photographs that they would miss the most, they were part of fires that killed three people and left a damage bill of A$10 million. Page 1.

A third person has taken advantage of the Northern Territory's euthanasia laws, yet very little has been released about the death. The patient was a 69-year-old man with terminal stomach cancer, and the death was reported only on the Internet. Under the Territory law, only the number of people to die under the legislation needs to be reported - all details apart from the death need not be disclosed. Page 1.

Australia's highest paid woman in television, Jana Wendt, will no longer head the Seven network current affairs show Witness, and while Seven says she will remain with them, her legal advisers claim Seven breached terms of her employment contract, and it's believed she has lodged an Industrial Court writ against Seven. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Federal Government wants to overhaul native title legislation and may need to amend the Racial Discrimination Act to be able to circumvent the High Court Wik ruling. Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday the current system of native title is "unworkable" and legislation may be brought in to extinguish common law rights established by the Wik ruling, a move that would not be tolerated by Aboriginal leaders. Page 1.

Australia was divided over the Wik case yesterday, as the country's political leaders met in Sydney, and Aboriginal leaders met in Cairns to discuss the native title issue. While the fallout from the Wik case is high on Prime Minister John Howard's agend, compromise will be necessary between governments and indigenous people to ensure the advances towards reconciliation in recent years are not lost. Page 1.

New South Wales Police Commissioner Peter Ryan yesterday called for a meeting with Aboriginal leaders to discuss the situation in the Sydney suburb of Redfern, where crime has increased by 40 per cent and the damage bill from this crime is costing the comunity "thousands of dollars". Ryan says the situation has become intolerable. Page 1.

New South Wales Community Services Minister Ron Dyer said yesterday, in reaction to a scathing report by the Council on the cost of government, that a cohesive team would be put in place to run the State's Department of Community Services. The report found senior management to be divided into factions over support for former Director-General Des Semple, and poorly informed. Page 3.
THE AGE

Police are investigating one of three fires that swept through the Dandenong Ranges on Tuesday. The fire hit Ferny Creek and killed Graham and Jennifer Lindroth and their next-door neighbour, and is believed to be an act of arson. The investigation could become a murder probe. Page A1.

The Mansfield report into the ABC, which is due tomorrow, will be used by the Federal Government to pave the way for further cuts in the broadcaster's budget, according to Cabinet documents obtained by the Age. The documents outline a strategy by Communiations Minister Richard Alston to give the ABC a narrower focus on a budget as little as A$416 million a year. Page A1.

Two victims of the bushfires in the Dandenong Ranges in Victoria, Graham and Jenny Lindroth of No. 29 Seabreeze Avenue, Ferny Creek, were mourned by their friend Andrew Raper whom both had completed horticulture apprenticeships with. Neighbours spoke of days spent frantically defending homes from the raging fires. Page A1.

Mornington Peninsula Shire Council has refused permission to trucking magnate Lindsay Fox to build a two-storey home near the water's edge at Point King Beach in Portsea. The plan had been opposed by local residents on environmental and lifestyle grounds with the council basing its decision on local clifftop residential zoning requirements. Page A3.
